title: My trusted adult network
subject: PSHE
label: Public edition
objective_verbatim: Map my network of trusted adults.
assessment_verbatim: F: scenario sorting.  S: 'my trusted network' + safe/unsafe task (Dec).

sources.note: Current main bytes match the accepted unchanged source; workbook not redistributed.
W3 16–20 Nov; W4 23–27 Nov. One lesson weekly per line; no day or slot inferred.

external_sources.title: Childline: Asking an adult for help
external_sources.supports: Choose a trusted adult, plan a message, use speech or a note, and seek another adult if needed. Adults may need to share a safety concern with people who can help.

external_sources.title: PSHE Association: Handling complex issues safely
external_sources.supports: Use ground rules, distanced examples, a right to pass and appropriate safeguarding responses.

evidence.description: A learner-owned network map using roles, with a first adult, backup, access route and reason; record whether it is personal or fictional practice.
evidence.status: contribution to source assessment; no completion claim

routes.Independent: Independent: map roles and how to reach them.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: explain a backup for a closed setting.

vocab.definition: Someone whose actions help us feel safe.
People or routes we can turn to.
Another option if the first is not there.
Shared only with people who need to know.

cases.text: An adult listens and takes a worry seriously.
cases.next_step: Ask for help in a quiet place.
cases.staff_note: Listening and appropriate action matter more than a job title or friendly manner.

cases.text: An adult says you must keep being hurt a secret.
cases.fact: The adult asks for a harmful secret.
cases.staff_note: Do not role-play this as an adult threat. Keep the example brief; no disclosure is required.

cases.text: The teacher is away. Another known staff member is at the office.
cases.next_step: Ask that staff member for help.
cases.staff_note: Staff identify the real available route privately before teaching.

cases.text: An adult explains who needs to know so they can help keep you safe.
cases.staff_note: Do not promise total secrecy. Follow the setting safeguarding procedure.

cases.text: A friendly online stranger asks for your address to help.
cases.fact: The person and purpose are not known.
cases.next_step: Do not share it. Ask a trusted adult.
cases.staff_note: A friendly message is not proof of trust. Do not open a live account in class.

cases.text: Sam cannot think of anyone to ask. Sam shows a help card to staff.
cases.fact: Staff can help find a safe route.
cases.next_step: Ask staff to identify an available adult.
cases.staff_note: No pupil is required to invent a supportive family member. Check a real route privately.

Purpose and success checks
Who can help me feel heard and safe?

Before pupils arrive

Print the Evidence Sheet, role/action cards and vocabulary. Before teaching, identify an available staff member and a private help route. Provide blank paper, pens and a calm space. No pupil contact list or online account is needed.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.

Access and practice
Supported: choose two adult roles. Independent: map roles and how to reach them. Aspire: explain a backup for a closed setting.

Model Sam’s map, sort A–F, then invite a role-only personal map or fictional practice. Complete the first adult, backup and access-route fields. Staff discreetly help anyone with no safe route rather than requiring a public explanation.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

Use Sam or role labels. Do not display or collect addresses, phone numbers, family histories or personal network names in a public pack. Offer a private alternative and a pass. If a concern is shared, listen without investigating, follow local safeguarding procedures and keep that record separate from learning evidence.
Assessment and feedback

Accept accessible adult roles and a workable way to reach them, with a reason based on listening, boundaries and helpful action. A role alone does not guarantee trust. A fictional map shows the mapping skill; do not label it a confirmed personal network. Staff check a real help route privately without demanding names or personal histories.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school's evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Speaking listening and writing

Explain a trusted action, listen to another option and ask for a private conversation. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio; no communication criteria are assigned here.

Model and hinge

Sam picks a school adult who listens. Sam can ask at the school office. A club leader is another option. If one adult is away, Sam asks another. A trusted adult takes concerns seriously. They may share a concern to get safe help.

Individual evidence key

Accept accessible adult roles and a workable way to reach them, with a reason based on listening, boundaries and helpful action. A role alone does not guarantee trust. A fictional map shows the mapping skill; do not label it a confirmed personal network. Staff check a real help route privately without demanding names or personal histories.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: Listening and appropriate action matter more than a job title or friendly manner.
Card B: Do not role-play this as an adult threat. Keep the example brief; no disclosure is required.
Card C: Staff identify the real available route privately before teaching.
Card D: Do not promise total secrecy. Follow the setting safeguarding procedure.
Card E: A friendly message is not proof of trust. Do not open a live account in class.
Card F: No pupil is required to invent a supportive family member. Check a real route privately.
Common misunderstandings

A trusted adult is not simply any adult, a relative or someone friendly. Asking another person is allowed if the first is unavailable or unhelpful. Private does not mean a promise that a safety concern will never be shared.
Teaching boundary

Use Sam or role labels. Do not display or collect addresses, phone numbers, family histories or personal network names in a public pack. Offer a private alternative and a pass. If a concern is shared, listen without investigating, follow local safeguarding procedures and keep that record separate from learning evidence.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
